# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

# [ufo] recent context, ⟦CMEM_NOW_HEADER:e54711a5c70e⟧

Fetch details: get_observations([IDs]) | Search: mem-search skill

Stats: 4 obs (1,684t read) | 36,504t work | 95% savings

### Nov 3, 2026
4 7:50p ○ cleanDoubleSlashes has no respectQueryAndFragment option; trailing-slash helpers already do
5 " ○ cleanDoubleSlashes collapses slashes per "://"-separated segment, including query and hash
6 " ○ Trailing-slash helpers implement respectQueryAndFragment by splitting off the fragment and query
7 " ◆ cleanDoubleSlashes gains opt-in respectQueryAndFragment flag that leaves query and hash untouched
S3 Add an opt-in `respectQueryAndFragment` flag to `cleanDoubleSlashes` so that `//` inside the query string and hash is preserved, with default behaviour unchanged and tests added. (Nov 3, 7:50 PM)
**Investigated**: Grepped for `cleanDoubleSlashes` and `respectQueryAndFragment` across `src` and `README.md`. Read the trailing-slash helpers in `src/utils.ts`, the `cleanDoubleSlashes` implementation, its README entry, and the existing table-driven tests in `test/double-slash.test.ts`.

**Learned**: The trailing-slash helpers (`hasTrailingSlash`, `withoutTrailingSlash`, `withTrailingSlash`) already use a `respectQueryAndFragment` flag. Their opt-in branch splits off the fragment and query before editing the path. The original `cleanDoubleSlashes` splits on `://` and collapses slashes in every other segment, so query and hash text was affected.

**Completed**: `cleanDoubleSlashes(input, respectQueryAndFragment?)` now accepts the flag. When true, only the portion before the first `?` or `#` is cleaned, so `/foo//bar?redirect=//baz` becomes `/foo/bar?redirect=//baz`. The default is unchanged. The old logic moved into a private helper, `_cleanDoubleSlashes`. JSDoc and the README entry were updated. New tests in `test/double-slash.test.ts` cover `?`, `#`, both together, full URLs with a protocol, input with no query or fragment, leading `?` or `#`, and a default-still-cleans check. The double-slash test file passes (13 of 13) and `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors. The full test suite was not run. Nothing has been committed.

**Next Steps**: No work is currently in progress. The session may receive further requests. Any follow-up would likely involve running the full test suite or committing the change.

**Notes**: The feature is scoped to the first `?` or `#`, so any `//` in the path after a query marker is also left alone. The full suite has not been run, so regressions outside the double-slash tests are unverified.
